provenance.method: lesson notes written from the NERDC 2025 scheme of work outline; every week keeps its scheme topic and bullets as the teaching spine

topics.title: Art: drawing with shapes
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to identify basic shapes.
The pupils should be able to draw a house and car using shapes.

Introduction:
We have learned about shapes in mathematics. Today we will use these shapes to create drawings.

Content:
Basic shapes include circle, square, triangle and rectangle. We can use these shapes to draw objects like houses and cars. For example, a square with a triangle on top makes a house. A rectangle with circles below makes a car. We can colour our drawings with our favourite colours.

Class activity:
Each pupil will draw a house and a car using basic shapes and then colour them.

Evaluation questions:
What shapes do we use to draw a house?
How many wheels does your car drawing have?
What colour is your house?

Summary:
We can use shapes to create drawings of objects like houses and cars.

topics.title: Art: patterns
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to identify different patterns.
The pupils should be able to create patterns on a shirt.

Introduction:
We see patterns in our clothes and in nature. Today we will learn to create our own patterns.

Content:
Patterns are repeated designs. Common patterns include stripes, dots and zigzag. Stripes are straight lines going up and down. Dots are small circles. Zigzag is a line that goes up and down like a mountain road. We can create beautiful patterns on a shirt to make it look nice.

Class activity:
Each pupil will draw a shirt outline and decorate it with different patterns.

Evaluation questions:
What are the three patterns we learned today?
How many stripes are on your shirt?
What pattern do you like most?

Summary:
Patterns can make our clothes look beautiful and interesting.

topics.title: Music: rhythm clapping
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to clap simple beats.
The pupils should be able to perform echo clapping.

Introduction:
We hear music everywhere, even in our clapping hands. Today we will learn about rhythm through clapping.

Content:
Rhythm is the beat of music. We can make rhythm by clapping our hands. Simple beats are like the sound of a danfo moving on the road. Echo clapping means one person claps and another person repeats the same clap. We can make patterns with our claps like clap-clap-pause-clap.

Class activity:
The class will form a circle and practice echo clapping with the teacher leading.

Evaluation questions:
What is rhythm?
How many claps are in a simple beat?
What happens in echo clapping?

Summary:
We can create music and rhythm just by clapping our hands.

topics.title: Art: colour wheel
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to identify primary and secondary colours.
The pupils should be able to mix colours to create new colours.

Introduction:
We see colours everywhere around us, from the Nigerian flag to our school uniforms. Today we will learn about how colours are made.

Content:
Primary colours are red, yellow and blue. These colours cannot be made from other colours. Secondary colours are made by mixing two primary colours. Red and blue make purple. Blue and yellow make green. Red and yellow make orange. We can mix colours like mixing kerosene and water to see what new colour we can create.

Class activity:
Each pupil will mix primary colours to create secondary colours on paper.

Evaluation questions:
What are the three primary colours?
What colour do we get when we mix red and blue?
How many secondary colours are there?

Summary:
We can mix primary colours to create new and beautiful secondary colours.

topics.title: Music: school songs
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to sing two school songs.
The pupils should be able to sing in parts.

Introduction:
We sing songs during assembly and in our music class. Today we will learn to sing school songs together.

Content:
School songs are special songs we sing at school. They teach us about our school and our country. We can sing songs like our national anthem and school anthem. Singing in parts means some pupils sing one part and others sing a different part, like when we play in the compound with different teams.

Class activity:
The class will divide into two groups and practice singing a school song in parts.

Evaluation questions:
What is your favourite school song?
How many parts are we singing in today?
Why do we sing school songs?

Summary:
Singing school songs together helps us learn about our school and our country.

topics.title: Art: clay work
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to mould a pot from clay.
The pupils should be able to smooth and paint the clay pot.

Introduction:
People in Nigeria have been making clay pots for many years to carry water and cook food. Today we will learn to make our own clay pots.

Content:
Clay is soft earth that we can shape with our hands. To make a pot, we roll the clay into a ball and then push our thumb in the middle to make a hole. We pinch the clay between our fingers to make the walls of the pot. After shaping, we smooth the clay with water to make it nice. Then we let it dry and paint it with our favourite colours.

Class activity:
Each pupil will mould a small pot from clay, smooth it, and paint it when dry.

Evaluation questions:
What is clay used for in Nigeria?
How do we make the hole in the pot?
What do we do to smooth the clay?

Summary:
We can create beautiful pots from clay by shaping, smoothing and painting them.

topics.title: Drama: role play
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to act as community helpers.
The pupils should be able to demonstrate proper stage manners.

Introduction:
In our community, we see many people who help us like teachers, doctors and farmers. Today we will act like these community helpers.

Content:
Community helpers are people who help us in our daily lives. They include teachers who teach us, doctors who care for our health, and farmers who grow our food. When we act on stage, we need good manners. We should speak clearly, face the audience, and wait for our turn to speak. This is called stage manners.

Class activity:
Each pupil will choose a community helper to act out in front of the class.

Evaluation questions:
Who is a community helper in your community?
What should we remember when acting on stage?
How do teachers help us?

Summary:
We can learn about community helpers by acting like them with good stage manners.

topics.title: Art: collage
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to create a paper collage of Nigeria.
The pupils should be able to use green and white colours in their collage.

Introduction:
Our national flag has green and white colours that represent our country. Today we will make a collage of Nigeria using these colours.

Content:
A collage is a picture made by sticking different pieces of paper together. Nigeria has many symbols we can include in our collage like the map shape, national flag and cultural symbols. The green colour in our flag represents our fertile land and white stands for peace. We can cut green and white paper to make our collage of Nigeria.

Class activity:
Each pupil will create a paper collage of Nigeria using green and white paper.

Evaluation questions:
What is a collage?
What do the green and white colours in our flag represent?
What symbol of Nigeria will you include in your collage?

Summary:
We can create a beautiful collage of Nigeria using green and white paper.

topics.title: Music: local instruments
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to identify local instruments like drum, shekere and flute.
The pupils should be able to play a simple beat on the drum.

Introduction:
Nigeria has many traditional instruments that make beautiful music. Today we will learn about some of these instruments.

Content:
Local instruments are musical instruments from our culture. The drum is a hollow wooden instrument we hit with our hands or sticks. The shekere is a dried gourd covered with beads that we shake. The flute is a long pipe we blow into to make music. These instruments are played during festivals and celebrations like New Yam festival.

Class activity:
The class will take turns playing a simple beat on the drum.

Evaluation questions:
What is a shekere made from?
How do we play the flute?
What festival do we play these instruments?

Summary:
Local instruments like drums, shekere and flute are important parts of Nigerian music.

topics.title: Revision and exhibition
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to display their art works.
The pupils should be able to perform in a class concert.

Introduction:
We have learned many things in cultural and creative arts this term. Today we will show what we have learned.

Content:
An exhibition is when we show our art works to others. We can display our drawings, clay pots and collages. A class concert is when we perform music and drama for our classmates and teachers. We can sing the songs we learned and act the role plays we practiced. This helps us share what we have learned with everyone.

Class activity:
The class will organize an exhibition of their art works and a small concert of their music and drama performances.

Evaluation questions:
What art work are you most proud of?
What song will you sing in the concert?
How do you feel about showing your work to others?

Summary:
We can share our learning through an exhibition and class concert.
